title: Toward Equitable Low-Carbon Mobility: Fairness-Aware Demand Prediction for Expanding Bike-Sharing Systems
abstract: arXiv:2608.26451v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Bike-sharing systems are an important component of low-carbon urban mobility, but continued expansion creates challenges in both cold-start prediction and equitable resource allocation. Newly deployed stations lack historical ridership records, causing a mismatch between training and inference for graph-based models on evolving networks. Historical demand may also encode structural inequalities, as lower ridership in low-income neighborhoods can reflect limited infrastructure access rather than weak latent demand. Models trained directly on such data may therefore reinforce existing mobility disparities. We propose FairGIN, a fairness-aware graph neural network for demand prediction in expanding bike-sharing systems. FairGIN integrates three components. translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.26451v1 公告类型：新 摘要：共享单车系统是低碳城市出行的重要组成部分，但持续扩展带来了冷启动预测和公平资源配置方面的挑战。新部署的站点缺乏历史骑行记录，导致图模型在演化网络上的训练与推理不匹配。历史需求也可能编码结构性不平等，因为低收入社区的低骑行量可能反映基础设施访问受限，而非潜在需求薄弱。直接基于此类数据训练的模型可能因此加剧现有的出行差异。我们提出FairGIN，一种用于扩展共享单车系统需求预测的公平感知图神经网络。FairGIN整合了三个组件：扩展模拟增量训练在训练期间随机模拟网络扩展，以减少冷启动分布差距；基于注意力的知识转移结合了...
tldr: 本文提出FairGIN，一种公平感知图神经网络，通过模拟扩展训练和注意力知识转移，解决共享单车扩展中的冷启动预测和公平性问题，避免加剧出行不平等。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes FairGIN, a fairness-aware graph neural network that addresses cold-start prediction and equity issues in expanding bike-sharing systems via expansion simulation training and attention-based knowledge transfer, preventing reinforcement of mobility disparities.
